faq: Where do the test questions come from?
From your real emails, chats, tickets and search terms, with names removed if you prefer. If you have few, we write realistic questions and label them clearly as invented.
Will you fix what you find?
Yes, in the Standard and Premium packages, for fixes to content and instructions. Changes that need a different chatbot tool or a new build are listed and can be quoted.
Can you test a chatbot built elsewhere?
Usually. We need a way to send questions and read answers, and permission from whoever owns it. We confirm what is possible before you order.
How do I know it is good enough to launch?
You get a scorecard and sign-off checklist. A good score is a sign, not a promise, so we also recommend watching the first week of real chats and tuning again.

desc:
Chatbot testing and tuning before launch checks your assistant against real customer questions and fixes the weak answers. Ecom Swift LLC runs the tests, marks each reply, corrects the content and instructions, and retests so you can see the change.

## Why does a chatbot need testing before launch?

A chatbot needs testing because a demo only shows the questions the builder thought of. Real customers write in fragments, misspell product names, ask two things at once and bring topics nobody planned for. A bot that answers five tidy test questions perfectly can still fail the sixth real one.

The cost of finding out after launch is higher. Wrong answers reach real customers, who may act on them, complain or leave. Testing first moves those mistakes to a safe place, where they can be fixed without anyone noticing.

## What testing on real questions reveals

Tests built from your actual emails, chats and tickets reflect how your customers truly speak. When we run them, three kinds of problems usually appear. Some answers are simply wrong, often because content is outdated or two sources disagree. Some are incomplete, giving half of what the customer needs. And some are confident replies to questions the bot should have declined or passed to a person.

Each group has a different fix. Wrong answers need content corrections. Incomplete ones need fuller entries. Over-confident ones need clearer instructions and refusal rules. Knowing which is which is the point of marking every answer instead of just checking a few.

## How tuning improves the outcome

Tuning is the repair step. We change the content the bot uses, the instructions it follows and the rules for when it should hand off. Then we run the same questions again. The difference between the first and second run shows what improved and what still needs attention.

This matters because small changes can have side effects. A fix for one topic may break another. Retesting with the same set catches that. Keeping the test set afterwards gives you a quick way to check the bot again whenever you change a policy or add content.

## What a thorough chatbot test includes

- Questions collected from your real emails, chats and tickets.
- A spread of easy, tricky and off-topic questions.
- Each answer marked as right, partly right or wrong.
- A ranked list of the weakest areas.
- Questions on prices, policies and dates, where mistakes cost the most.
- Safety checks for refusals, such as requests the bot must decline.
- Checks that handoff works when a customer asks for a person.
- Fixes applied to content, instructions or rules.
- A retest, with before and after results side by side.
- A sign-off checklist your team can use before launch.

## What we do

We collect questions from the sources you give us and add a set of difficult cases of our own: ambiguous wording, mixed requests and subjects outside your business. Then we run every question against your chatbot and record the answers in a simple sheet.

The Basic package tests a set of real questions and delivers a results sheet with the top weak spots. The Standard package tests more, includes tricky and off-topic questions, makes a set of fixes and retests with before and after scores. The Premium package tests the widest set, adds safety tests, makes more fixes, provides a sign-off checklist and leaves you with the test set for future checks.

We can test a chatbot built by someone else, as long as we have access to try it. We cannot promise that no wrong answer will ever appear, since customers always find new questions. What we can show is how the bot performs on a fair sample of what they really ask.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Use real customer wording, including typos and short messages.
- Include questions the bot should refuse.
- Fix the content first and the instructions second.
- Retest after every change.
- Agree in advance what a passing result looks like.

**Avoid:**
- Testing only with questions written by the builder.
- Ignoring partly right answers because they look fine.
- Launching on the day the last fix is made, with no retest.
- Treating a perfect score on a small test as proof.
- Skipping safety checks for refusals and handoff.

## Who this service is for

It suits a business about to launch a chatbot that wants confidence first. It suits an owner whose bot is already live and suspected of giving odd answers. It also suits an agency that built a bot for a client and wants an independent check.

## What we need from you

Send examples of real questions, or access to the places they live, such as a shared inbox export. Tell us which topics are most sensitive. We need access to the chatbot as a team member or collaborator in order to run the tests and make fixes. We never ask for passwords.
